subject: Clarifying consent capture, subprocessors, and ingress/egress controls for PHI handling
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@lighthousehealth.org>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@lighthousehealth.org>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions on consent capture and subprocessors (Lighthouse RFP section 3.2)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We're progressing through the RFP and the security/compliance questionnaire and have a couple of items we need clarified before legal will sign off on the BAA. Two specific asks from our Privacy and Security teams:

1) Consent capture model: We need to understand whether Redwood stores any raw consent tokens or PII tied to end-user consent receipts. If you persist consent metadata, what fields are retained and for how long?

2) Subprocessors and data flow: The questionnaire asks for a list of subprocessors involved in PHI processing and whether any third parties receive PHI in cleartext (ingress/egress points). Please confirm whether any Google/AWS managed services you use can read PHI in transit or at rest.

If you can point us to a small data flow diagram and a sample consent matrix that maps which data elements are retained vs ephemeral, that would be very helpful.

Appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday if possible — our contract slot is tight.

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@lighthousehealth.org>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@lighthousehealth.org>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on consent capture and subprocessors (Lighthouse RFP section 3.2)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; attaching a redwood_data_flow_diagram.pdf and a draft consent_matrix.xlsx for your privacy team to review. If anything needs more detail we can schedule a short walkthrough.

1) Consent capture model:
- Redwood does not persist end-user consent tokens tied to raw PHI.
- We store consent metadata (consent_granted: Boolean, consent_source: e.g., "app", "portal", timestamp, and consent_scope labels) for audit and routing decisions.
- Consent metadata is retained by default for 365 days; customers may configure retention down to 0 days via their tenant settings.
- We never store the full content of a signed consent form unless the customer explicitly uploads it as an attachment to their account (those uploads follow our standard encrypted object storage lifecycle).

2) Subprocessors and ingress/egress controls:
- Primary subprocessors: AWS (S3 for object storage), GCP (optional private cloud regions customers choose), FastBatch Inc. (inference optimization partner for dedicated pools). A full, current subprocessors list is in the attached data flow diagram and our public Subprocessors page (link in footer).
- PHI in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced across all endpoints; we do not route plaintext PHI through external logging services.
- PHI at rest: Data in our primary object storage is encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) when customers enable Private deployment or KMS integration; hosted customers get our platform-managed encryption keys by default.
- No subprocessors have access to decrypted PHI outside of the runtime required to serve inference requests. We use ephemeral in-memory buffers and strict memory zeroing post-request.

Attachments: redwood_data_flow_diagram.pdf (high-level mapping) and consent_matrix.xlsx (sample mapping of data elements to retention and processing purposes).

Quick ask: can your privacy team confirm whether the retention configurable to 0 days satisfies your policy for not retaining consent metadata? If not, what is the target retention window? That will help us prepare BAA language.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Manager, Compliance & Solutions
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@lighthousehealth.org>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on consent capture and subprocessors (follow-up)

Hi Lauren / Rishi,

Thanks for the prompt write-up and the attachments — the diagram helps. A couple of follow-ups from our technical reviewers:

- Subprocessor detail: For FastBatch Inc. we need an SLA statement confirming they operate exclusively within encrypted enclaves and that they do not log input payloads. Can Redwood provide a short subprocessors attestation?

- KMS control: When customers enable KMS/HSM, is key rotation customer-controlled or can Redwood rotate keys on behalf of the customer? We need to be explicit in the BAA about key custody and access during emergency troubleshooting.

- Ingress/egress audit: Can Redwood produce an exportable ingress/egress audit for a configurable time window (start/end) that includes source IP, destination, and service component that handled the data? We want a sample log extract for validation.

Attached is a preliminary consent_matrix.xlsx with Lighthouse-specific retention expectations (we marked several items as 0 days). If Redwood can confirm technical feasibility of those retention flags, we can move to redlining the BAA.

Thanks,
Lighthouse Security Team
security@lighthousehealth.org

[attachment: lighthouse_consent_matrix_review.xlsx]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lighthouse Security Team <security@lighthousehealth.org>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:57:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on consent capture and subprocessors (next steps and BAA draft)

Team — internal note (dropping action items and proposed language for BAA):

1) FastBatch subprocessors attestation: Rishi, can you ask our partner ops to provide an attestation. We need a short statement confirming no persistent logs of input payloads and enclave-only processing. If FastBatch cannot provide that, we will need to add a BAA-approved subprocessors clause that requires specific operational controls.

Proposed attestation language for BAA (for legal to review):
"FastBatch Inc., when acting as a subprocessor for Redwood Inference, processes customer PHI solely within encrypted execution environments. FastBatch does not persist or retain input payloads beyond ephemeral processing buffers, and does not export decrypted input data to external observability platforms. Redwood Inference requires and audits this behavior as part of its vendor management program."

2) KMS rotation: Grace — short answer: customers maintain key ownership & rotation when they configure customer-managed KMS. Redwood can optionally rotate platform-managed keys but only with explicit customer consent documented in the BAA. Add clause: "Customer retains exclusive control over key rotation when customer-managed KMS is enabled; Redwood will not access plaintext without documented emergency access procedures."

3) Ingress/egress audit log: Aditya — please confirm whether the runtime emits structured audit events including source IP, component, and operation id. We should be able to export a zipped CSV for a given time range. If not, identify the time and engineering scope to provide a 30-day window export.

Action items: Rishi (partner attestation), Aditya (audit extract capability), Grace (KMS clause text). I will prepare a BAA redline (baa-draft-v3.docx) incorporating these bullets and share with Lighthouse by EOD Friday.

Best,
Lauren
Sr. Manager, Compliance & Solutions
Redwood Inference
